title: Unit Testing with Jest & React Testing Library
description: Write reliable unit tests for components, hooks, and data fetching – your safety net for refactoring.

slides.title: Why Unit Tests? 🧪
slides.content:
# Confidence When Changing Code

Unit tests verify that a small piece of code (a function, a component) behaves as expected.

* Catch regressions early.
* Document expected behavior.
* Enable fearless refactoring.

Next.js works seamlessly with **Jest** (test runner) and **React Testing Library** (component renderer).

slides.title: Setup: Install & Configure (Terminal)
slides.content: Add Jest, React Testing Library, and the Next.js Jest plugin.
slides.codeSnippet:
npm install --save-dev jest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom jest-environment-jsdom
# Optional: TypeScript types
npm install --save-dev @types/jest

quizData.question: What is the philosophy of React Testing Library?

options.text: Test implementation details like state and props
Test components as the user would interact with them (by role, text, label)

quizData.explanation: React Testing Library encourages tests that resemble how users find and interact with elements, making tests more resilient.

slides.title: Jest Config (jest.config.js)
First Component Test (__tests__/Button.test.js)
slides.content: Test a simple button renders and handles click.

quizData.question: What does `screen.getByText('Click me')` return?

options.text: The DOM element containing the text, or throws an error if not found

quizData.explanation: `getByText` queries the DOM for an element with the given text and returns it. If not found, it throws immediately.

slides.title: Testing Data Fetching with MSW 🎭
Testing a Page with MSW (__tests__/PostsPage.test.js)
slides.content: Mock the fetch and test that the list renders.

quizData.question: Why use MSW instead of mocking `fetch` directly?

options.text: It intercepts real network requests at the service worker level, providing more realistic tests
It only works on the server

quizData.explanation: MSW simulates a real HTTP server, so your code uses actual `fetch` calls without modification, making tests closer to production.

slides.title: Testing Best Practices ✨
slides.content: Focus on behavior, not implementation. Test what the user sees and does. Use `findByText` for async elements. For Server Components, you can import and await them directly in tests (they are just functions).
